title: vLLM Engine
description: vLLM's native metrics (vllm:*) scraped from every Ray Serve replica: requests, latency, tokens, engine iterations, KV and prefix cache, health and capacity. Installed by llm-deployment/scripts/deploy.sh.

panels.title: Replicas scraped / Serve RUNNING
panels.description: Scraped: vLLM metrics endpoints whose last scrape succeeded (sum of up). Serve RUNNING: replicas Ray Serve's health checks report RUNNING (llm_sd_replicas, from Serve's REST API). Scrape health is not inference readiness: compare both, and use ./scripts/chat.sh for an end-to-end check.

panels.title: Arrivals / s
panels.description: API requests reaching the replicas (llm_serve_requests_received_total, counted on arrival by the Serve app; vLLM 0.6.6 has no arrival counter).

panels.title: Completions / s
panels.description: Requests vLLM finished (vllm:request_success_total, all finish reasons). Requests rejected before reaching the engine or aborted by a disconnecting client are not included.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Requests in vLLM's running batch (vllm:num_requests_running), summed over replicas. Updated on engine steps: after traffic stops it keeps the value of the last step.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: Requests queued in vLLM's scheduler (vllm:num_requests_waiting). Requests beyond max_ongoing_requests wait in Ray Serve instead and are not counted here.

panels.title: p95 time to first token (5m)
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])))

panels.title: Generated tokens / s
panels.description: rate(vllm:generation_tokens_total), all replicas.

panels.title: Max KV cache usage
panels.description: Highest vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc of any replica (fraction of GPU KV-cache blocks in use).

panels.title: Arrivals vs completions (fleet)
panels.description: Arrivals: llm_serve_requests_received_total (Serve app, on arrival). Completions: vllm:request_success_total (engine). Errors: llm_serve_responses_total with a non-2xx code, including 499 (client disconnected). A lasting gap between arrivals and completions is a backlog or failures.

panels.title: Completions by finish reason
panels.description: vllm:request_success_total by finished_reason: stop (EOS or stop string), length (max_tokens or context reached).

panels.title: Running requests per replica
panels.description: vllm:num_requests_running per replica, against vLLM's max_num_seqs limit.

panels.title: Waiting requests per replica
panels.description: vllm:num_requests_waiting per replica: queued in vLLM because the batch (max_num_seqs) or the KV cache is full.

panels.title: Responses by HTTP status
panels.description: llm_serve_responses_total by code, as answered by the replicas (499 = the client went away mid-stream). Errors in Ray Serve's proxy before a replica is reached are in the Ray Serve dashboards.

panels.title: Time to first token
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero. Measured inside vLLM from the request entering the engine: includes vLLM queueing and prefill, not Ray Serve's proxy or tokenization. Buckets top out at 10 s.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Inter-token latency (time per output token)
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero. vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds: the gap between consecutive tokens of a request while decoding. Buckets top out at 2.5 s.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: End-to-end request latency
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero. vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds: request entering the engine to its last token; grows with output length. Buckets top out at 60 s.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Queue time
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero. vllm:request_queue_time_seconds: time a request spent WAITING in vLLM's scheduler.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_queue_time_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_queue_time_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_queue_time_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(vllm:request_queue_time_seconds_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:request_queue_time_seconds_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Prefill vs decode time (p95)
panels.description: Fleet percentiles: every replica's bucket rates are summed by le first, then histogram_quantile runs once - replica percentiles are never averaged. Mean = rate(sum) / rate(count). With no finished requests in the window the result is empty (a gap), not zero. vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds and vllm:request_decode_time_seconds per finished request.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_decode_time_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Tokens per request (mean)
panels.description: Mean prompt and generated tokens per finished request (vllm:request_prompt_tokens and vllm:request_generation_tokens histograms, rate(sum) / rate(count)). Use it to read end-to-end latency, which scales with output length.

targets.expr: sum(rate(vllm:request_prompt_tokens_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:request_prompt_tokens_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum(rate(vllm:request_generation_tokens_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(vllm:request_generation_tokens_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: p95 time to first token per replica
panels.description: Each replica's own p95, from its own buckets (sum by instance, le). Compare replicas here; for the fleet use the fleet panels, never an average of these.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p95 inter-token latency per replica
panels.description: Each replica's own p95, from its own buckets (sum by instance, le). Compare replicas here; for the fleet use the fleet panels, never an average of these.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p95 end-to-end latency per replica
panels.description: Each replica's own p95, from its own buckets (sum by instance, le). Compare replicas here; for the fleet use the fleet panels, never an average of these.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (instance, le) (rate(vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Prompt and generated tokens / s (fleet)
panels.description: rate(vllm:prompt_tokens_total) - prefill tokens processed - and rate(vllm:generation_tokens_total).

panels.title: Generated tokens / s per replica
panels.description: rate(vllm:generation_tokens_total) per replica.

panels.title: Tokens per engine iteration (not batch size)
panels.description: vllm:iteration_tokens_total is a histogram of tokens processed in one engine step: prompt (prefill) tokens plus one token per decoding sequence. It is NOT the number of requests in the batch - one long prefill can be thousands of tokens from a single request. Its buckets are vLLM's CUDA-graph batch sizes (largest usually 256), so steps with more tokens land in +Inf and percentiles are capped at the largest bucket: trust the mean. Per replica: mean = rate(sum) / rate(count).

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(vllm:iteration_tokens_total_sum{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (instance) (rate(vllm:iteration_tokens_total_count{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:iteration_tokens_total_bucket{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Batch occupancy (running requests / max_num_seqs)
panels.description: Request batch size relative to vLLM's limit: vllm:num_requests_running / max_num_seqs per replica. This counts requests (sequence groups), unlike tokens per iteration. Sampled at engine steps.

targets.expr: vllm:num_requests_running{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"} / on (instance) group_left llm_serve_max_num_seqs{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Engine iterations / s
panels.description: Engine steps per second per replica (rate of the iteration histogram's count).

panels.title: GPU KV cache usage per replica
panels.description: vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc: fraction of GPU KV-cache blocks in use (1 = full). Near 1 with waiting requests or preemptions means the KV cache is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Preemptions / s
panels.description: rate(vllm:num_preemptions_total): requests evicted from the KV cache to make room (recomputed or swapped later). Sustained preemption wastes GPU time and inflates latency.

panels.title: Swapped requests
panels.description: vllm:num_requests_swapped: requests whose KV cache was moved to CPU memory (V0 engine).

panels.title: Prefix cache hit ratio from counters: not supported by vLLM 0.6.6

options.content:
A windowed hit ratio needs prefix-cache **hit and query counters** (`rate(hits) / rate(queries)`). vLLM **0.6.6.post1**, which this deployment pins, does not export them; they arrive with the V1 engine in later vLLM releases. Nothing here is computed from them, and missing series are not treated as zero.

What 0.6.6 does export is the gauge `vllm:gpu_prefix_cache_hit_rate`, shown to the right:

- **Unit:** fraction (0-1) of KV-cache *block* lookups that hit, not tokens and not requests.
- **Window:** cumulative since the replica started; it does not reflect the last minutes.
- **-1** means prefix caching is off - the V0 default. Enable it with `./scripts/deploy.sh --engine-arg enable_prefix_caching=true`.
- It cannot be combined across replicas (no query counts to weight by), so it is shown per replica only.

panels.title: GPU prefix cache block hit rate per replica (lifetime gauge)
panels.description: vllm:gpu_prefix_cache_hit_rate, filtered to >= 0 (-1 = prefix caching disabled). Cumulative since replica start, block granularity. Empty when prefix caching is off.

panels.title: Metrics scrape health per replica
panels.description: Prometheus up for each vLLM metrics endpoint (1 = last scrape succeeded). This is scrape health only: a replica can answer /metrics while its engine is failing, or be serving while the scrape fails. Readiness is the Serve replica states panel.

panels.title: Serve replica states (readiness)
panels.description: Replicas of the application by state, from Ray Serve's REST API via the llm-metrics-sd service (llm_sd_replicas). RUNNING = passing Serve's health checks, which call vLLM's check_health.

panels.title: KV cache headroom (tokens)
panels.description: Free GPU KV-cache capacity per replica: (1 - vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc) x llm_serve_kv_cache_capacity_tokens (num_gpu_blocks x block_size).

targets.expr: (1 - vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance) group_left llm_serve_kv_cache_capacity_tokens{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Free batch slots
panels.description: max_num_seqs - vllm:num_requests_running per replica: requests the engine could still add to its running batch (KV cache permitting).

targets.expr: llm_serve_max_num_seqs{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"} - on (instance) vllm:num_requests_running{job="vllm", application=~"$application", deployment=~"$deployment", model_name=~"$model", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Ray Serve in-flight vs limit (fleet)
panels.description: ray_serve_replica_processing_queries (Ray Serve, via Ray's metrics agent) against the sum of max_ongoing_requests over replicas. At the limit, Serve queues new requests before they reach vLLM - that queue is invisible to vLLM's metrics. Ray can keep exporting a replaced replica's last value for a while.

panels.title: Scrape duration per replica
panels.description: scrape_duration_seconds of each vLLM metrics endpoint. Rising values mean a busy replica process (the endpoint shares the replica's Python process).

panels.title: Firing vLLM alerts
panels.description: Prometheus' ALERTS series for the rules in llm-deployment/observability/vllm (no Alertmanager: nothing is sent anywhere). Full list: Prometheus :9090/alerts.
